result.summary: This PR moves per-peer transaction relay state (bloom filter, tx inventory queue, send scheduling) out of net_processing.cpp into a new node::TxRelay class with private, TSA-annotated fields, and only then replaces the two RecursiveMutex members with plain Mutex. It adds a TxInventoryBatch snapshot mechanism so SendMessages() can process queued inventory without holding TxRelay's mutex, plus new unit tests and a fuzz target for the extracted class. Part of the long-open issue #19303 to eliminate RecursiveMutex usage across the codebase.
result.problem: Peer::TxRelay previously exposed its RecursiveMutex-guarded state directly to net_processing.cpp, so 18 call sites locked and mutated it ad hoc. That made it unsafe to simply swap RecursiveMutex for Mutex, since external code could recurse or take locks out of order, a concern maintainers (sedited, maflcko) raised directly.

resolved_concerns: sedited's early 'brittle' concept-ack concern was answered by a broader encapsulation refactor rather than a minimal mutex swap.

maflcko's objection that exposing GetBloomFilterMutex()/GetTxInventoryMutex() and a callback-under-lock pattern undid the safety of the private-field approach was addressed by removing the public getters and the WithBloomFilterIfSet() callback, replaced by TxRelay::MakeMerkleBlock(); pablomartin4btc confirmed this addressed the concern and maflcko has not followed up since 2026-06-20.
A silent merge conflict noted by sedited on 2026-06-29 was resolved by a rebase on 2026-06-30/07-01.

result.card: This PR encapsulates Peer::TxRelay's per-peer transaction-relay state into a new node::TxRelay class with private, Clang-TSA-annotated locking, then replaces its two RecursiveMutex members with plain Mutex, as part of the long-standing issue #19303 to eliminate RecursiveMutex usage. The problem it solves is that net_processing.cpp previously locked and mutated TxRelay's guarded state directly from ~18 call sites, making a bare mutex-type swap unsafe against lock-order violations or accidental recursion. The strongest evidence of importance is maflcko's sustained objection that a naive swap 'risks unsafe code down the line,' which the author resolved by removing public mutex getters and a callback-under-lock pattern in favor of TxRelay::MakeMerkleBlock() and EXCLUSIVE_LOCKS_REQUIRED-annotated methods, after which pablomartin4btc and sedited re-ACKed. The PR is currently Ready for review, with clean CI and an author who has actively iterated through nine force-pushes addressing review feedback, most recently a 2026-09-15 rebase. It has no hard dependency on other open PRs but is explicitly one step in the broader #19303 mutex-safety project.
